chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Olive Burgorne and Black women performers who became maids
summary: Dave Nelson's wife Olive Burgorne was a former dancer who, like other old Black performers, worked as a maid for white stars.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, that was Harry White. Then I lay off a couple of weeks out of the Nest Club, and Dave Nelson, he goes in there. Now, when I got in there with him... His wife is Miss Olive Burgorne(?), who had been a dancer and a singer ways years ago, had toured Russia with a Black group, she was high in show business, and yet she was relegated now to doing maid work, like a lot of old Black woman performers became maids to White stars who knew them -- and they knew show business. So they hired these women, because women knew how to keep their mouths closed and knew all the intrigue of how to keep...how to answer the phone and how to keep one Stage-Door Johnny from bumping into the husband, or... It's an intrigue thing. So they kept all these slick Black women as maids.

And they was part of the theatre, and they kept in the background -- but they loved the Theatre. Just to be there in the footlights. That's a science to be explained in itself, about how these women, dedicated stage-

door people, who handled show people and who were showmen, who are telling you, you know, "Don't be afraid; this is your opening night," encourage the young performers. "Just go on out there and kill 'em and slay 'em, look 'em in the eye" -- give you all that kind of encouragement. So they kept them...
